senses.gloss:
भ्रशिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, (superl.) most powerful,
very strong or violent, very vehement.

भ्रशिष्ठ भ्रशिष्ठ, भ्रशीयस्. See under
rt. भृश्, p. 721, col. 1.

भ्रशीयस्, आन्, असी, अस्, (compar.) more powerful,
stronger, more violent or vehement, very vehement.

भ्रंश् भ्रंश् or भ्रश् (sometimes written
भ्रंस्; cf. rt. भृश्), cl. 4. P. भ्रश्-
यति (ep. also भ्रश्यते, &c.), cl. 1. A. भ्रंशते,
बभ्रंश, बभ्रंशे, भ्रंशिष्यति, -ते, अभ्र-
शत्, अभ्रंशिष्ट, भ्रंशितुम्, Indec. part. भ्रं-
शितुआ or भ्रष्ट्वा, to fall, tumble, drop or fall
down, fall out; to decline, decrease, decay, fade,
disappear, vanish, to be ruined or lost; to fall from,
stray from, be separated from, be deprived of, lose
(with abl.); to run away, flee from (with abl.):
Caus. भ्रंशयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अबभ्रंशत्, to
cause to fall, throw or cast down, precipitate; to
[]
ruin, overturn, expel; to cause to be lost, cause to
disappear or vanish; to cause to be separated from,
deprive of (with acc. of person and abl. of thing):
Desid. बिभ्रंशिषति, -ते: Intens. बाभ्रश्यते,
बाभ्रष्टि, बनीभ्रश्यते, बनीभ्रंशिति, बनी-
भ्रंष्टि; [cf. Angl. Sax. hreosan, resosan, ‘to
fall;’ arisan, ‘to rise:’ Goth. ur-risan, us-hris-
jan, af-hrisjan, ‘to cast off.’]
भ्रंस् भ्रंस्. See rt. भ्रंश्, col. 1.

भ्रंश, अस्, m. falling, falling off, a fall; de-
clining, decline, decrease; decay, overthrow, destruc-
tion, ruin (e. g. देश-भ्˚, ruin of a country); dis-
appearance; running away; separating from, aban-
doning, deserting; losing, loss [cf. जाति-भ्˚]; de-
viating or straying from (propriety &c.).
भ्रंशथु, उस्, m. = प्र-भ्रंशथु, q. v.

भ्रंशित, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. the Caus.), made to
fall, thrown down.

भ्रंशिन्, ई, इनी, इ, falling, tumbling, falling
down, falling out, falling from or off, coming to
ruin, decaying; causing to fall, ruining, annihilating;
[cf. स्वार्थ-भ्˚.]

भ्रष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, fallen, dropped, fallen
down, fallen out or off; declined, decayed, ruined,
disappeared, lost; fallen from, strayed from (with abl.,
e. g. सार्थाद् भ्रष्ट उष्ट्रः, a camel strayed
from a caravan); separated from, deprived of (with
abl.); depraved, vicious, a backslider; (आ), f. a fallen
or unchaste woman.
—भ्रष्ट-क्रिय, अस्, आ, अम्,
one who has discontinued or omitted prescribed acts.
—भ्रष्ट-गुद, अस्, आ, अम्, suffering from pro-
lapsus ani.
—भ्रष्ट-निद्र, अस्, आ, अम्, deprived
of sleep.
—भ्रष्ट-योग, अस्, आ, अम्, one who
has fallen from devotion, a backslider.
—भ्रष्ट-
राज्य, अस्, आ, अम्, fallen from or deprived of a king-
dom.
—भ्रष्टाधिकार (˚ट-अध्˚), अस्, आ, अम्,
fallen from office, deprived of office.
—भ्रष्टा-
धिकार-त्व, अम्, n. loss of office.

भ्रष्ट भ्रष्ट, भ्रष्टक. See p. 724,
col. 2.

भ्रष्टक, अस्, m., N. of a man; (आस्), m. pl.,
N. of his descendants.

भ्राश्य, अस्, आ, अम् (fr. Caus. of rt. भ्रश् or fr. rt.
भ्राश् ?), Ved. to be made to fall, to be struck down;
(according to Sāy. on Ṛg-veda X. 116, 5, भ्रा-
श्यानि = आयुधानि, ‘weapons,’ and connected with
rt. भ्राश्, to shine.)
भ्राश्य भ्राश्य. See p. 724, col. 2.

भ्रकुंश भ्रकुंश or भ्रकुंस, अस्, m. an
actor in female apparel; [cf. भृकुंश, भ्रुकुंश,
भ्रूकुंश.]

भ्रकुटि भ्र-कुटि or भ्र-कुटी = भ्रू-कुटि,
इस्, f. a contraction of the eyebrows, frown.
—भ्र-
कुटि-मुख, अम्, n. a face with contracted eyebrows,
frowning face, (also written भृकुटी-मुख.)
भ्रक्ष् भ्रक्ष्. See rt. भृक्ष्, p. 720.

भ्रज् 1. भ्रज् in गिरि-भ्रज्, q. v.; (the word
भ्रज् is thought to be fr. a lost rt. भ्रज् = Lat.
frango.)

भ्रज् 2. भ्रज्, f., Ved. (perhaps) stiffness;
[cf. मृत-भ्˚.]

भ्रज्ज् 1. भ्रज्ज् (in the Dhātu-pāṭha writ-
ten भ्रस्ज्; cf. rt. भृज्), cl. 6. P. A.
भृज्जति, -ते (for भर्जते, see rt. भृज्), बभ्रज्ज,
बभर्ज्ज, बभ्रज्जे, बभर्ज्जे, भ्रष्टा, भर्-
ष्टा, भ्रक्ष्यति, -ते, भर्क्ष्यति, -ते, अभ्रा-
क्षीत्, अभार्क्षीत्, अभ्रष्ट, अभर्ष्ट, भ्रष्-
टुम्, भर्ष्टुम्, to fry, broil, grill, parch, scorch,
roast (especially grain): Pass. भृज्ज्यते: Caus.
भ्रज्जयति, भर्ज्जयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अब-
भ्रज्जत्, to fry, roast: Desid. बिभ्रक्षति,
-ते, बिभर्क्षति, -ते, बिभ्रज्जिषति, -ते [cf. बि-
भ्रक्षु, बिभ्रज्जिषु]; Intens. बरीभृज्ज्यते,
बाभ्रष्टि or बाभर्ष्टि (?); [cf. Gr. φρῡ́γ-ω,
[]
φρύγ-ανο-ν, φρύγ-ε-τρο-ν, φρυκ-τό-ς; Lat. frīg-0,
frictus, frixus; Old Germ. briuwan = Angl. Sax.
briwan = Old Iceland. brugga = Eng. brew; Hib.
bruighim, ‘I boil, seeth.’]

2. भ्रज्ज्, भ्रट्, ट्, ट् (or भृट्, ट्, ट्, if fr.
भृज्ज्, q. v.), frying, roasting, (at the end of a
comp., e. g. धाना-भ्˚, roasting or parching grain,
see Pāṇ. VIII. 2, 36.)

भ्राज् 1. भ्राज् (connected with rts. राज्,
भ्राश्, भ्लाश्, भ्रेज्, भृज्), cl. 1. A.
भ्राजते (Ved. and ep. also P. भ्राजति), बभ्राजे
(बभ्राज) or भ्रेजे (3rd pl. बभ्राजिरे or भ्रे-
जिरे, Pāṇ. VI. 4, 125), भ्राजिष्यते, अभ्राजिष्ट
(Ved. अभ्राट्, अभ्राजि), भ्राजितुम्, to shine, glitter,
gleam, glow, flash, beam, sparkle: Caus. भ्राज-
यति, -यितुम्, Aor. अबभ्राजत्, अबिभ्रजत्, to
make to shine, illuminate, irradiate: Desid. बिभ्रा-
जिषते: Intens. बाभ्राज्यते, बाभ्राष्टि; [cf. Gr.
φλέγ-ω, φλεγ-έ-θ-ω, φλέγ-μα, φλεγ-μονή, φλεγ-υρό-ς,
φλύξ: Lat. fulg-e-o, fulg-ur, ful-vu-s, flag-
ra-re, flam-ma for flag-ma, flā-men for flag-men,
‘the kindler, i. e. priest:’ Goth. bairh-t-s, ‘mani-
fest;’ bairhtei, ‘light:’ Angl. Sax. bearht, beorht,
probably blāc, blœc-an, blīc-an: Old Germ.
beraht, blanch, blich-an, blich, blic, blig: Engl.
bright: Russ. blescu: Lith. blizg-ù, ‘I shine:’
Scot. breagh, ‘shining, beautiful;’ breachad, boillsg,
‘splendor;’ boillsgeach, ‘splendid.’]

2. भ्राज्, भ्राट्, f. (Pāṇ. VIII. 2, 36), Ved. light,
lustre, splendor, glitter; [cf. देव-भ्˚, न-भ्˚.]

भ्रज्जन, अम्, n. the act of frying, parching,
roasting; [cf. भृज्जन, भर्जन.]

भ्राजन, अम्, n. (fr. the Caus.), the act of
causing to shine, illuminating.

भ्रष्टव्य, अस्, आ, अम्, to be fried, to be
parched or roasted.

भ्रष्टव्य भ्रष्टव्य, भ्रष्ट्र. See p. 724,
col. 3.
भ्रष्ट्र, अम्, n. a frying-pan, gridiron.

भ्राष्ट्र, अस्, अम्, m. n. a frying-pan; (अस्),
m. light, ether (in this sense probably to be con-
nected with rt. भ्राश्); (अस्, ई, अम्), fried or cooked
in a frying-pan.
—भ्राष्ट्र-ज, अस्, आ, अम्, pro-
duced or cooked in a frying-pan; (आ), f. a pan-cake
made of rice-flour.
—भ्राष्ट्रम्-इन्ध, अस्, आ, अम्,
heating the frying-pan, one who fries or cooks.
—भ्राष्ट्र-व्रतिन्, ई, m. N. of a man.

भ्राष्ट्र भ्राष्ट्र, भ्राष्ट्रक. See p. 724,
col. 3.
भ्राष्ट्रक, अस्, अम्, m. n. a frying-pan.

भ्राष्ट्रकि, इस्, m., N. of a man, (also read
भ्राष्ट्र-कृत्.)

भ्रण् भ्रण् [cf. rts. भ्रम्, रण्], cl. 1.
P. भ्रणति, बभ्राण, भ्रणितुम्, to
sound, utter a sound.

भ्रभङ्ग भ्र-भङ्ग, अस्, m. = भ्रू-भङ्ग
under भ्रू, p. 726, col. 2.

भ्रम् भ्रम्, cl. 1. 4. P. (ep. also A.)
भ्रमति (-ते), भ्राम्यति (-ते; accord-
ing to Pāṇ. III. 1, 70, a form भ्रामति is admis-
sible; the form भ्रम्यति is doubtful), बभ्राम
(2nd sing. बभ्रमिथ or भ्रेमिथ, 3rd pl.
बभ्रमुस् or भ्रेमुस्), भ्रमिष्यति, अभ्र-
मीत्, भ्रमितुम् or भ्रान्तुम्, (perhaps orginally)
to fly about humming (as insects); to roam or
wander about, rove or ramble about, go or move
about, (भिक्षाम् भ्रम्, to go about begging);
to stroll, perambulate; to circulate, revolve, turn or
whirl round, move in a circle or orbit, move round
(as the stars &c.); to totter, stagger about, waver;
to go astray, stray, deviate (from rectitude), err, be
in error or mistake, be perplexed, be foolish or
ignorant; to move to and fro, move unsteadily,
flicker, flutter, vibrate, quiver (as the tongue, eyes,
flames, &c.); to surround; to roam or wander
through, go over (with acc., e. g. देशम् भ्रम्, to
wander through a country): Caus. भ्रमयति,
भ्रामयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अबिभ्रमत्, to cause
or make to wander, make to rove or roam; to
cause to turn round or revolve; to whirl round,
swing; to cause to roll or roll along or through;
to cause to err, delude, perplex, embarrass, con-
fuse, seduce; to cause to move to and fro, wave,
brandish, agitate, vibrate: Pass. of Caus. भ्राम्-
यते, to be made to wander or whirl, caused to err,
made to go astray: Desid. बिभ्रमिषति: Intens.
बम्भ्रम्यते, बम्भ्रमीति, बम्भ्रान्ति, to
roam about repeatedly, move frequently to and fro,
wander through; [cf. Gr. βρέμ-ω, ὑψι-βρεμ-έ-της,
βρόμ-ο-ς, βρον-τή, βαβράζω, πεμφρηδών, φριμάσσομαι,
φόρμιγξ, ῥέμβω;Lat. frem-o, frem-or,
frem-itu-s; Old Germ. brem-an, bremo, briosa;
Angl. Sax. bremman; Old Iceland. brim, ‘surf.’]

भ्रम, अस्, m. roving or roaming about, wan-
dering about; moving or going round, turning
round, whirling, revolving, moving or going to and
fro; straying, erring; a flickering flame (Ved.);
a circular motion, whirl; a whirlpool, eddy; a
potter's wheel; a lathe; a grindstone; giddiness,
dizziness; wandering of mind; confusion, perplexity,
error, mistake, aberration, misconception, misappre-
hension, delusion [cf. स्थाणु-भ्˚]; a spring, foun-
tain, watercourse; (आत्), ind. by an error or mistake.
—भ्रम-त्व, अम्, n. whirling found, the being
[]
in error or mistake, erroneousness.
—भ्रमासक्त
(˚म-आस्˚), अस्, m. ‘occupied in grinding,’ a knife-
grinder, sword-cleaner, armourer.

भ्राम, अस्, m. roaming about, wandering, un-
steadiness, delusion, error, mistake.

भ्रमण, अम्, n. (fr. the simple rt. or Caus.),
the act of roaming, wandering about, travelling, tour-
ing, a tour; turning round, whirling; revolution,
the orbit (of a planet &c.); wavering, staggering,
tottering, shaking about, unsteadiness, deviation
(from rectitude); causing to go round or move
about; erring, falling into error; giddiness, dizzi-
ness; (ई), f. a sort of game (played by lovers, pro-
bably consisting in circular movements or waltzes);
a leech; N. of one of five Dhāraṇās or mental con-
ceptions of the elements (viz. that of the wind; the
others being स्तम्भिनी, earth; धारिणी, water; द-
हनी, fire; and शोषिणी, ether).
—भ्रमण-विल-
सित, N. of a metre.
—भ्रमणार्थे (˚ण-अर्˚),
ind. for the sake of travelling.

भ्रामण, अम्, n. the act of causing to turn
round, swinging or turning round; (ई), f. ‘the be-
wilderer,’ N. of a female demon.

भ्रमणीय, अस्, आ, अम्, to be roamed about, to
be wandered through.

भ्रमत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, roaming, roving, prowl-
ing, wandering, sauntering about, turning round,
whirling, shaking, &c.
—भ्रमत्-कुटी, f. a sort of
umbrella, a concave mat carried on the head; [cf.
जङ्गम-कुटी.]

भ्रममाण, अस्, आ, अम्, wandering about,
whirling round; being in error.

भ्रमर, अस्, m. a large black bee, a kind of
humble bee, any bee; a lover, gallant, libertine; a
young man; a potter's wheel; a particular position
of the hand; N. of a man; (आ), f. = भ्रमर-
च्छल्ली below; (ई), f. a bee; the plant Jatukā,
q. v.; the plant Putra-dātrī, q. v.; (अम्), n. giddi-
ness, vertigo, epilepsy.
—भ्रमर-करण्डक,
अस्, m. a small box containing bees (used by thieves
to extinguish a candle-light by letting the bees
escape), a dark lantern (?).
—भ्रमर-कीट, अस्,
m. a species of wasp that builds its nest in the
corners of walls, doors, &c., Vespa Solitaria.
—भ्र-
मर-कुण्ड, N. of a sacred bathing-place on the
mountain Nīla (mentioned in Raghu-nātha's Rasika-
ramaṇa).
—भ्रमर-च्छल्ली, f. a species of creeper
(= भृङ्ग-मूलिका, भृङ्गाह्वा, भ्रमरा).
—भ्रमर-पद, अम्, n. ‘bee-foot,’ a kind of
metre, four times ¯˘˘¯˘¯˘˘˘˘˘˘˘˘˘¯¯¯.
—भ्रमर-प्रिय, अस्, m. ‘dear to bees,’ a par-
ticular sort of Kadamba plant (= धारा-कदम्ब).
—भ्रमर-बाधा, f. annoyance caused by a bee,
molestation by a bee.
—भ्रमर-मण्डल, अम्,
n. a circle or swarm of bees.
—भ्रमर-मारी, f.
‘bee-killing,’ a particular plant or flower (growing
in Malwa, = भृङ्ग-मारी, भ्रमरारि).
—भ्र-
मर-विलसित, अस्, आ, अम्, (a creeper, lotus, &c.)
about which bees hover or sport; (अम्), n. the
hovering or sporting of bees; (आ, अम्), f. n. a species
of metre, four times ¯¯¯¯, ˘˘˘˘˘˘¯.
—भ्र-
मरातिथि (˚र-अत्˚), इस्, m. ‘bee-guest,’ the plant
Michelia Champaka.
—भ्रमरानन्द (˚र-आन्˚),
अस्, m. ‘bee-joy,’ N. of several plants, Mimusops
Elengi, Gærtnera Racemosa (= अतिमुक्तक), the
red-flowering globe amaranth (= रक्ताम्लान).
—भ्रमराम्बा-क्षेत्र (˚र-अम्˚), अम्, n., N.
of a district sacred to Durgā; [cf. भ्रामरी, अम्बा.]
—भ्रमरारि (˚र-अरि), इस्, m. ‘bee-enemy’ (=
भ्रमर-मारी, q. v.).
—भ्रमरालक (˚र-
अल्˚), अस्, m. ‘bee-curl,’ a curl on the forehead.
—भ्रमरावली (˚र-आव्˚), f. ‘bee-line,’ N. of a
species of the Ati-śakkarī metre.
—भ्रमराष्-
टक (˚र-अष्˚), अम्, n. ‘eight verses on the bee,’
N. of a collection of eight verses.
—भ्रमरेष्ट
(˚र-इष्˚), अस्, m. ‘loved by bees,’ a sort of Big-
nonia; (आ), f. the plant Clerodendrum Siphonanthus
(= भूमि-जम्बू, q. v.).
—भ्रमरोत्सवा (˚र-
उत्˚), f. ‘bee-delight,’ the plant Gærtnera Racemosa
(= माधवी).

भ्रामर, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. भ्रमर), relating
or belonging to a bee; (अस्, अम्), m. n. a kind of
magnet or loadstone [cf. भ्रामक]; (अम्), n.
whirling round; dancing round; vertigo, giddiness,
epilepsy; honey; a village; a kind of coitus; (ई),
f. an epithet of Durgā or Pārvatī (from her having
assumed the form of a bee to contend with Mahi-
ṣāsura ?); a Yoginī or female attendant on Durgā.

भ्रमरक, अस्, m. a bee; a whirlpool; (अस्,
अम्), m. n. a lock of hair or curl hanging down on
the forehead; a humming-top; a ball for playing
with; (इका), f. the act of wandering or straying in
all directions.
—भ्रमरिका-दृष्टि, इस्, f. a wan-
dering glance (?).

भ्रमाय (fr. भ्रमत्, see Gaṇa Bhṛśādi to
Pāṇ. III. 1, 12), Nom. A. भ्रमायते, &c., (pro-
bably) to begin turning round or revolving; to roam
about, become a vagabond.

भ्रमि, इस् (according to some also भ्रमी), f.
whirling or turning round, turning about, going
round, circulating, revolving [cf. संवत्सर-भ्˚];
a potter's wheel, a turner's lathe; a whirlpool; a
whirlwind; any circular arrangement of troops, a cir-
cle formed by troops; an error, a mistake; N. of a
daughter of Śiśu-māra and wife of Dhruva.

भ्रमित, अस्, आ, अम्, whirled round, made to
go round, &c.

भ्रमिन्, ई, इणी, इ, roaming about, going round
or about, whirling round, revolving, making a circuit,
turning round (as the wind), erratic.
भ्रामिन्, ई, इणी, इ, confused, perplexed.

भ्रान्त, अस्, आ, अम्, roamed, wandered (some-
times impersonally, e. g. तैर् भ्रान्तम्, it has
been wandered by them; and even with acc., e. g.
देशम् भ्रान्तम्, it has been wandered through a
country); whirled round, turned round, revolved,
rolled; confused, perplexed, bewildered, gone astray,
mistaken, in error, blundering; roaming or wander-
ing about, turning round, whirling, rolling, stagger-
ing, flying or careering round and round (as a bird),
moving to and fro; (अस्), m. an elephant in rut; a
species of thorn-apple, = राज-धुस्तूरक; (अम्),
n. roaming, wandering about, moving to and fro; a
particular mode of fighting; error, mistake, delusion,
blunder.
—भ्रान्त-चित्त, अस्, आ, अम्, confused or
perplexed in mind.
—भ्रान्त-बुद्धि, इस्, इस्, इ,
confused in intellect, perplexed in mind, puzzled.

भ्रान्त भ्रान्त, भ्राम, भ्रामर, भ्राम्-
यत्, &c. See p. 725, col. 2.

भ्रान्ति, इस्, f. the act or state of wandering about,
roaming, going round, flying about, turning round,
revolution, whirling, rolling, a whirl or rapid rotary
motion; confusion, perplexity, delirium [cf. मति-
भ्˚]; error, going astray, mistake, delusion, false
idea or supposition, wrong notion (e. g. पद्म-
भ्रान्त्या, under the false idea of [its being] a lotus;
भ्राह्मण-भ्रान्ति, the error of supposing [those
works to be] Brāhmaṇas); unsteadiness; doubt, un-
certainty.
—भ्रान्ति-कर, अस्, ई, अम्, causing error
or confusion.
—भ्रान्ति-नाशन, अस्, m. ‘destroying
error,’ an epithet of Śiva.
—भ्रान्ति-मत्, आन्, अती,
अत्, wandering or roaming about, whirling; erring,
mistaken, being under a delusion, labouring under
an error; entertaining a false notion; a particular
figure of rhetoric (describing an error).
—भ्रान्ति-
हर, अस्, आ, अम्, taking away delusion, removing
error; (अस्), m. a counsellor, minister.

भ्रान्त्वा, ind. having wandered about, having
roamed through; having whirled.

भ्रामक, अस्, इका, अम् (fr. the Caus. or fr.
भ्रम), causing to whirl; causing error or mis-
take, bewildering, perplexing, puzzling, deceitful,
deceptive, false; (अस्), m. a sort of loadstone or
magnet (so called from its causing iron to turn
round); sun-flower, heliotrope; a deceiver, cheat,
rogue; a jackal; (आ), f., N. of a particular plant
(commonly called Laghu-dhāyaṭī).

भ्रामयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to turn round,
whirling round, bewildering.

भ्रामरिन्, ई, इणी, इ (fr. भ्रामर), whirling
round, revolving; affected with vertigo, giddy; hav-
ing epilepsy, epileptic; made of honey.

भ्राम्यत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, roaming or rambling
about, strolling about, perambulating; erring.

भ्राम्यमाण, अस्, आ, अम्, being caused to
wander about, being made to whirl round, being
caused to err or go astray.

भ्रमात्र भ्रमात्र, a particular high num-
ber.
भ्रश् भ्रश्. See rt. भ्रंश्, p. 724, col. 1.

भ्राश् भ्राश् (connected with rts. 1.
भ्राज्, भ्लाश्), cl. 1. 4. A. भ्राशते,
भ्राश्यते (Ved. also P. भ्राश्यति), बभ्राशे or
भ्रेशे (3rd pl. बभ्राशिरे or भ्रेशिरे, Pāṇ. VI.
4, 125), भ्राशिष्यते, अभ्राशिष्ट, भ्राशितुम्,
to shine, glitter, gleam, blaze: Caus. भ्राशयति,
यितुम्, Aor. अबभ्राशत्, अबिभ्रशत् (Vopa-deva
XVII. 3): Desid. बिभ्राशिषते: Intens. बाभ्राश्-
यते, बाभ्राष्टि.

भ्रास् भ्रास्, a various reading for rt.
भ्राश्, col. 1.

भ्रशिमन् भ्रशिमन्, आ, m. (fr. भृश), po-
tency, mightiness, vehemence, violence, excessive-
ness, strength.

भ्रस्ज् भ्रस्ज्. See rt. 1. भ्रज्ज्, p. 724,
col. 2.

भ्राज, अस्, आ, अम्, shining, gleaming, glittering
(Ved.); (अस्), m., N. of one of the seven suns; of
a particular kind of fire (mentioned in Hari-vaṃśa,
1. 10467); of a Gandharva protecting the Soma
(Ved.); of a work composed in Ślokas and ascribed
to Kātyāyana; (अम्), n., N. of a Sāman.

भ्राजक, अस्, इका, अम् (fr. the Caus.), causing
to shine, illuminating, making bright (said of the
digestive fire and bile as brightening the skin);
(अम्), n. the bile, bilious humor, gall.

भ्राजत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, shining, gleaming, glitter-
ing.
—भ्राजज्-जन्मन्, आनस्, m. pl., Ved. ‘having
a brilliant native place or origin, brilliant form birth,’
an epithet of the Maruts; (Sāy.) having brilliant
forms (= दीप्त-शरीर).
—भ्राजद्-ऋष्टि, अयस्,
m. pl., Ved. ‘bright-weaponed’ (having bright
gleams of lightning), an epithet of the Maruts;
(Sāy. = दीप्यमानायुध.)

भ्राजथु, उस्, m. brilliance, splendor, glitter,
beauty.
—भ्राजथु-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, shining,
beautiful (said of a woman).
भ्राजमान, अस्, आ, अम्, shining, brilliant.

भ्राजयत्, अन्, अन्ती, अत्, causing to shine, illu-
minating.

भ्राजस्, अस्, n., Ved. sparkling, glittering; [cf.
अग्नि-भ्˚.]
—भ्राजस्-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. spark-
ling, glittering; containing the word भ्राजस्.
—भ्रा-
जस्-विन्, ई, इनी, इ, Ved. = भ्राजस्-वत् above.
भ्राजिन्, ई, इनी, इ, shining, gleaming, glittering.

भ्राजिर, आस्, m. pl., N. of a class of gods under
the Manu Bhautya.

भ्राजिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम् (superl. fr. rt. 1. भ्राज्),
[]
shining very brightly, highly glittering or radiant;
(अस्), m., N. of a son of Ghṛta-pṛṣṭha.

भ्राजिष्णु, उस्, उस्, उ, shining, gleaming, splen-
did, radiant, elegant; (उस्), m. an epithet of Viṣṇu;
of Śiva.
—भ्राजिष्णु-ता, f. radiance, brightness,
splendor, splendid appearance.

भ्राजिस्, इस्, f. = भ्राजस्, p. 725.
—भ्राजिष्-
मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, splendid, shining.
भ्राजोभ्रादन्त्य (?), आस्, m. pl., N. of a race.

भ्रातृ भ्रातृ, ता, m. (perhaps fr. rt. भृ,
and originally meaning ‘a supporter’), a brother,
uterine brother, own brother, (कु-भ्रातृ, a bad
brother); an intimate friend or relation, a cousin or
near relative in general, an intimate friend, (some-
times used as a term of friendly address); (तरौ),
m. du. brother and sister; [cf. Zend brātar: Gr.
φράτηρ, φράτωρ, φρᾱτρ-ία, φρᾱ́τρ-α or φρή-τρη,
φρατρίζ-ω, φρατριάζ-ω, φράτριοι θεοί: Lat. frāter,
fraternu-s, frātr-ia, ‘a brother's wife:’ Umbr. frā-
ter: Goth. brōthar, pl. bro-thra-hans, ‘brethren:’
Angl. Sax. bródhor: Old Germ. bruodar: Slav.
brātrŭ: Lith. broter-eli-s, a diminutive; bró-li-s,
‘brother;’ brotù-szi-s, ‘a cousin:’ Old Pruss. bra-
ti-s: Russ. brat: Hib. brathair.]
—भ्रातुर्-
जाया, f. (भ्रातुर्, gen. sing.), a brother's wife, sister-
in-law.
—भ्रातुष्-पुत्र, अस्, m. (भ्रातुष् for
भ्रातुस्, gen. sing.), a brother's son, nephew; (ई),
f. a brother's daughter, niece.
—भ्रातृ-गन्धि,
इस्, इस्, इ, or भ्रातृ-गन्धिक, अस्, आ, अम्, a brother
only in appearance, having merely the name of
brother.
—भ्रातृ-ज, अस्, m. a brother's son; (आ),
f. a brother's daughter.
—भ्रातृ-जाया, f. a brother's
wife, sister-in-law.
—भ्रातृ-त्व, अम्, n. fraternity,
brotherhood.
—भ्रातृ-दत्त, अस्, आ, अम्, given by
a brother; (अम्), n. anything given by a brother to
a sister on her marriage.
—भ्रातृ-द्वितीया, f. a
festival on the second day in the light half of the
month Kārttika (on which sisters give entertain-
ments to brothers in commemoration of Yamunā's
entertaining her brother Yama).
—भ्रातृ-पत्नी, f.
a brother's wife.
—भ्रातृ-पद्म-वन, अम्, n. a
group of lotus-like brethren.
—भ्रातृ-पुत्र, अस्,
m. a brother's son, nephew.
—भ्रातृ-भगिन्यौ,
du. a brother and sister.
—भ्रातृ-मत्, आन्, अती,
अत्, having a brother or brothers.
—भ्रातृ-वधू,
ऊस्, f. a brother's wife.
—भ्रातृ-वल, अस्, आ, अम्,
possessing a brother or brothers.
—भ्रातृ-श्व-
शुर, अस्, m. a husband's eldest brother.
—भ्रातृ-
सिंह, अस्, m., N. of a man.
—भ्रातृ-हत्या, f.
fratricide.

भ्रातृक, अस्, आ, अम्, having a brother, (at the
end of a comp., cf. अ-भ्˚); coming from a brother,
of or belonging to a brother, fraternal, brotherly (in
this sense the fem. is ई).

भ्रातृव्य, अस्, m. a brother's son, nephew,
cousin; a rival, enemy, adversary; [cf. Lat. fra-
trūelis.]
—भ्रातृव्य-क्षयण, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved.
destroying rivals.
—भ्रातृव्य-चातन, अस्, आ, अम्,
scaring or frightening away rivals.
—भ्रातृव्य-
वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, Ved. having rivals.
—भ्रातृव्य-
हन्, हा, घ्नी, m. f. killing or striking down rivals
(Atharva-veda X. 9, 1).
भ्रात्र, अम्, n., Ved. brotherhood, fraternity.

भ्रात्रीय or भ्रात्रेय, अस्, m. a (father's)
brother's son, nephew; (अस्, आ, अम्), fraternal, be-
longing or relating to a brother.
भ्रात्र्य, अम्, n. = भ्रात्र above.

भ्राष्ट्रेय भ्राष्ट्रेय, आस्, m. pl., N. of a
family or race; (also भ्रास्त्रेय.)
